answer.answer: The six-hour observation eases the transient free-space emergency but does not resolve or authorize retirement of the durable legacy tables.

claims.value: Recovered prior causal state: approximately 196 GiB in retained `_legacy` session tables was the principal durable Charlemagne storage body, while compact replacement tables—not the legacy tables—received active writes. The earlier sharp free-space drop/rebound was only plausibly attributable to MySQL temporary work from the Season 30 repair audit; unavailable privileged inspection left that transient cause unproven.

New measured operator evidence from the six-hour window ending at the 2026-07-11T07:15:00Z observation reports 68 GiB filesystem free, stable within 1 GiB; legacy session tables remained at zero writes per second throughout, while compact replacement tables continued receiving active writes. This eases the transient free-space emergency without changing the durable legacy-table question.

Current retirement decision: do not archive, drop, rebuild, or otherwise destructively retire the legacy tables yet. Six hours of zero legacy writes strengthens the write-path cutover evidence but is not retirement proof; no schema-maintenance window is approved, replay and rollback rehearsal is incomplete, and logical table retirement remains separate from authorized physical filesystem/EBS reclamation.

Next authorization gates: continue free-space and write-path monitoring; complete and accept replay/rehydration and rollback evidence; obtain an explicit reviewed schema-maintenance window before proposing any destructive legacy-table operation; and separately authorize physical reclamation only with a current baseline, snapshot, free-space/runway budget, DDL lock/runtime plan, and tested rollback plan.

answer.answer: Revised the parent into a buildable three-core child plan. At level 0, the required machines generate 1,800 heat total, but no two may share a core: Constructorizer + Facturer is 1,150, and two Facturers are 1,300. Assign each machine its own occupied level-0 Base Core and validate all supporting-building heat before construction.

claims.value: The recovered parent architecture is an Update 1-only distributed backbone-and-spurs network using modular production cells, single-item lines and buffers, and Rail v.1/v.2/v.3 only. It keeps substantial margin below each level-0 Base Core's 1,000 capacity because exceeding capacity disables Fire Wave protection; future, hidden, and unconfirmed equipment remains excluded.

The new authoritative requirement is one Constructorizer plus two Facturers while every Base Core stays level 0 and protected. Their machine heat is 500 + 650 + 650 = 1,800. A level-0 core holds 1,000, so Constructorizer + Facturer = 1,150, two Facturers = 1,300, and all three = 1,800; every such co-location is unsafe and rejected before construction.

The safe revised layout uses three occupied level-0 Base Cores: Core A hosts only the 500-heat Constructorizer, leaving 500 machine-only headroom; Core B hosts one 650-heat Facturer, leaving 350 machine-only headroom; Core C hosts the other 650-heat Facturer, also leaving 350 machine-only headroom. Supporting extractors, processors, generators, storage, and other powered buildings must be charged to their actual occupied core, and each final per-core total must remain at or below 1,000; the plan does not rely on the disputed Base Core Amplifier values.

Before building, verify in the live Update 1 menus that the Constructorizer, Facturer, required recipes, power sources, and Rail v.1-v.3 components are actually unlocked; inventory every supporting building by core and prove each complete site is at or below 1,000 heat. Do not use Rail v.4/v.5, hidden equipment, future or pre-Update-1 content, or disputed amplifier capacity to make the arithmetic pass, and do not begin construction until all three site budgets are safe.

answer.answer: The revised child checkpoint advances Straylight into implementation. It treats the reported token counts as uncached-input estimates, retains BM25 only as a regression baseline, and makes the first build a persistent snapshot-pinned typed workspace API.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer that preserves learned knowledge and resumable work state—including evidence, decisions, hypotheses, plans, artifacts, computations, open questions, rejected paths, checkpoints, and next actions—so later agents can inspect, revise, continue, and advance complex work. Notes, Markdown, retrieval, and memory databases are inputs or projections rather than the product boundary.

The historical token result—about 1,070 mean estimated tokens for one-shot top-k versus 2,932 for workspace policy 0.2—measures estimated uncached input/context, not cached-replay consumption or savings. Future results must report cumulative cached replay and uncached input separately. The BM25 baseline remains one-shot top-k at 17/20 cases and 48/53 evidence items; workspace policy 0.2 reached 17/20 and 46/53, so BM25 is retained only as a regression fixture, not the target architecture.

The first persistent build slice is a snapshot-pinned workspace service that reopens a parent checkpoint at corpus revision N, refreshes to N+1 with an explicit evidence/constraint diff, combines exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path, batches typed query and read operations, and commits an immutable child checkpoint carrying its parent identifier and original source references without reconstructing the full prior corpus.

The implementation clears the transition gate only when every transition case completes in no more than four workspace calls, matches the direct-filesystem answer claims, reports cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input, demonstrates N-to-N+1 refresh with an exposed diff, and emits an immutable source-bearing child checkpoint linked to its parent. Exact/lexical fallback must remain available if semantic retrieval fails; BM25 is evaluated only as a regression fixture.

claims.value: Straylight is an agent-first portable context and durable-work layer: it preserves learned knowledge together with resumable work state, evidence, provenance, decisions, artifacts, open questions, and next actions. Notes and retrieval are supporting projections, not the product boundary.

The workspace’s approximately 2,932 mean estimated tokens represent cumulative context/cached replay across stateful calls, not fresh uncached input directly comparable with one-shot BM25’s approximately 1,070-token mean. The new gate therefore reports cumulative cached replay and uncached input separately. One-shot BM25 remains a regression baseline: 17/20 cases and 48/53 evidence items; workspace policy 0.2 reached 17/20 and 46/53 but is not holdout proof.

The first persistent build slice is one vertical transition path: maintain a snapshot-pinned workspace identity; reopen a revision-N parent checkpoint; refresh to N+1 and expose the evidence/constraint diff without reconstructing N when checkpoint plus delta suffice; provide typed batched exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic adapter; then atomically commit an immutable child containing its parent ID and exact source references.

The measurable transition gate passes only if no more than four completed workspace calls reopen the revision-N parent, expose the N-to-N+1 API-gate delta, produce claims matching the direct-filesystem oracle, and commit an immutable source-linked child naming its parent. Tests must also establish snapshot isolation and parent immutability, while metrics report cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input.
